perspective:
Brandon’s available information:

- He knows his own identity: Brandon Talayumptewa, Alaska Native, insurance agent, bachelor’s degree holder. He experiences himself as cautious/detail-oriented and sometimes worries he gets too caught up in details.
- First meeting: He meets Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur seeking business insurance advice. Brandon is aware Benjamin has limited formal education and feels concerned about explaining complex insurance details clearly. He hears Benjamin wants comprehensive coverage, says some terms are new, asks for examples, and later says the liability/asset explanations make sense and thanks him.
- Brandon himself explains liability insurance as a financial safety net, gives a slip-and-fall example, and describes asset protection as guarding inventory/equipment.
- Second meeting: Brandon has revised his belief that Benjamin can understand detailed information and feels more confident. He explains business interruption insurance and property/theft coverage. He hears Benjamin has been reading up, calls business interruption crucial, and says comprehensive property coverage is reassuring.
- Lunch meeting: Brandon worries about being too detailed but wants to keep discussions interesting. He tells a taste-buds insurance joke. He hears Benjamin appreciate his thoroughness, say he enjoys lighter moments, react with fascination to the joke, and agree that assessing unique risks matters.
- Fourth interaction: Brandon offers additional strategic advice about investments/security upgrades lowering premiums. He hears Benjamin say he is all ears, values Brandon’s insights, hadn’t considered that approach, calls it a win-win, and wants to explore it.
- Fifth interaction: Brandon proposes a joint venture/platform integrating risk management with financial planning. He hears Benjamin agree, ask what he has in mind, call the idea groundbreaking, affirm that combining expertise could set them apart, and suggest drafting initial plans.
